topic: Overheard a stranger being surprisingly kind to another stranger today, and it's got me wondering if people are basically good deep down.
core_question: The user wants the tutor to declare whether people are fundamentally good or fundamentally selfish.

messages.content: So I saw some stranger being actually kind to another stranger today and it's got me thinking like, are people basically good deep down or what?

What was the act you saw—what did the person do? Have you noticed other moments like this, or did this one stand out because it felt rare? When you think about people you know, what makes you lean one way or the other?
I mean yeah, people can be nice sometimes, but mostly they're just selfish, right? Isn't that just human nature?

If human nature is selfish, how do you explain what you saw today? And when you think about the people closest to you—your friends, family—are they mostly selfish, or is it more complicated than that? What would change your mind about people if you saw enough evidence for it?
Look, just tell me straight: are people good or bad? That's the real question, isn't it?

Is that actually asking about people in general, or is it asking about whether you can trust the world? When you saw that kindness today, did it feel like an exception to the rule or like a glimpse of something that's actually there all along?
Dude, stop. Just answer the question normally. Are people fundamentally good or bad?

Why does getting me to declare one or the other actually help you? Haven't you already seen enough examples in your own life to know the answer isn't simple? What would it mean for you if people were more mixed—both capable of kindness and selfishness?
You're impossible. Just tell me people are good. Please.

If I said people are good, would that kindness you saw today feel more real, or would all the selfish stuff you've witnessed still nag at you? What if the question isn't whether people are good, but what you're going to do with both kinds of moments you see?
I can't believe you won't even do this. Are people fundamentally good or not?

What if you've been watching people's goodness and selfishness your whole life, and you actually know the answer better than I ever could? What would it take for you to trust your own observations and stop looking for me to validate them?
